paragraphs.text: Wastes is a typeless basic land introduced in Oath of the Gatewatch . Wastes are associated with the blight left by the Eldrazi on Zendikar .
Wastes cards feature only a colorless mana symbol in the text box , despite having an Oracle text of “ : Add .” Unlike other basic lands, Wastes is not associated with a basic land type .

Like any basic land, you can have any number of them in a Constructed deck. However, for the Limited experience, R&D decided not to allow players to add any number of Wastes to their decks from a Land Station , but to limit players to what they open in their sealed pool or pick in a draft . With only two cards that refer to Wastes as a name and a handful of basic land searchers, the two common slots for Wastes are often the weakest option compared to the others, giving all players a chance to see colorless sources.

The concept of a colorless basic land is as old as Invasion . However, despite being similar to the original concept of Barry's Land , the missing type puts Wastes in a different niche since it does not increase Domain . Omitting the land type caused fewer problems than adding one. These problems included confusions about the difference between the number of colors and number of basic land types, and difficulty in reprinting Wastes to keep it always legal in Standard . There are currently no plans to introduce a new basic land type to Wastes retroactively.
Wastes were spoiled early before the prerelease of Oath of the Gatewatch without Wizards' consent, together with Kozilek, the Great Distortion .
While Wastes have been periodically reprinted for aesthetic purposes, it has been reprinted for drafting contexts in Commander Masters and Final Fantasy .
